nodes.title: 2026-10-20 — AI gateway, wired into `codex/`

nodes.text: - **Only `codex/` uses the gateway.** `claude/` is unchanged, and its `just claude` server doesn't load the keys.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Not done yet:** CSP/COOP/COEP headers (2.1), per-user key store (2.9), token budgets and cost display (2.11), structured output for board annotations (2.7).
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **NDJSON over `fetch` instead of SSE (2.8).** `EventSource` can't POST a body, and a JSON-lines stream over `fetch` gives cancellation through `AbortController` for free.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Newer Node treats `node --test <dir>` arguments as file patterns,** so the test script needs a glob.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Live checks found account problems, not code problems.** The OpenAI key was rejected (401). The Mistral key was refused `mistral-large-latest` by subscription tier (403), then rate-limited (429). A 403 doesn't necessarily mean a bad key, so `auth_failed` now says "check the key and that your plan includes the model".
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Haiku 5.5 gave coaching as good as Opus 5.5 on a simple question**, at a fraction of the cost. The engine supplies the hard part. This supports small models by default; worth confirming on harder positions with the tutor eval set (3.8).
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text:
- **The gateway is a spending proxy, so it needs browser-side guards even on localhost.**
  - Any website can POST to `127.0.0.1`, which is why the gateway requires JSON and checks `Origin`.
  - DNS rebinding can make a page from another site look local. Requiring `Host` to be `localhost` or an IP literal blocks that, because rebinding only works under a host name.
  - Both are covered by tests (OWASP A01, LLM10).
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-20 — AI provider layer: interface, structured output, models, limits, settings, contract tests

nodes.text: - **2.11 per-user limits and 2.9's per-user key store** wait for accounts (10.1).
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **2.15 stays open** until OpenAI, Mistral and Ollama fixtures are recorded.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **No built-in price list.** Prices change and I couldn't verify current ones, so cost needs `AI_PRICES`.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **No `stream` flag on `chat()`:** it always streams, and `complete()` collects the reply when a caller wants it whole.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Structured output uses JSON-schema output, not tool calling**, on every provider. It's the same mechanism everywhere, and no tool is involved.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Formats are named on the server.** The page can't send its own schema, which keeps model output bounded to what the server validates.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Usage, the budget and settings changes live in memory** and reset when the server restarts.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Claude's structured output accepts the stripped annotation schema natively.** The recorded reply validated first time, so the fallback is for the OpenAI-compatible servers whose models can't do JSON schema.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Replaying at the `fetch` level catches more than fake clients.** It covers the SDKs' own stream parsing and error classes; the fake-client unit tests stay for edge cases that are hard to record.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Strict JSON-schema modes reject some constraints.** Two layers keep it portable: what the provider sees, and what we enforce.
nodes.heading: Insights

Keep model IDs in config, never in code, and have the connection test (TODO 2.14) report which model actually answered.

nodes.title: 2026-10-20 — Fixes from the code review: bugs and security

nodes.text: - **`RULES` stays a user turn,** so the page keeps working with the artifact's `sample()`, which has no system role. The quoting carries the protection.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text:
- **Not fixed:**
  - Keyboard move entry (TODO 1.11).
  - PGN comments are still keyed by position, so repeated positions share one comment.
  - `renderAll` still recomputes more than it needs to (only the hidden panes are skipped).
  - Most of the inline script is still one module; only the engine, storage and prompt helpers moved out.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **COEP is not sent,** because it would need CORP headers on every resource; it's only needed for multi-threaded Stockfish (TODO 1.3).
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **chessground ignores untrusted (synthetic) mouse events** unless `trustAllEvents` is set. UI races are better reproduced with Playwright's fake clock (`page.clock`): it froze the 60 ms before the engine's reply, so the take-back race failed reliably on the old code.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **A file-writing tool turned the escapes ` `/` ` into the literal characters.** Inside a regex literal those are line terminators, which broke parsing. Keep such escapes ASCII and check with `node --check`.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **The mock provider made the prompt-injection test cheap:** the test intercepts the request to `/api/ai/sample` and checks exactly what the model would receive.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-20 — Foundation: tooling, CI, licence

nodes.text: - **E2E in CI uses Playwright's Chromium**, set with `PW_CHANNEL=chromium`. Locally the tests still use the installed Chrome.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **No npm workspaces (0.3).** Splitting `site/` into `client`, `server` and `shared` would move every file and the build paths, for no gain yet: the server doesn't import `knowledge.js`, and when it needs to, a relative import works. One project keeps one lockfile and one install. Revisit when the server needs its own deployable package (TODO 12).
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **No Prettier (0.5).** The code is written densely on purpose: one-line guards and short bodies on one line. Prettier at 120 columns turned the 2,136 lines in `src/` into 5,142 and touched nearly every line. ESLint checks correctness; `.editorconfig` covers whitespace.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **CodeQL is skipped while the repo is private.** Code scanning on private repos needs GitHub Advanced Security. The job has `if: !github.event.repository.private`, so it starts working once the repo is public. Secret scanning uses gitleaks instead of GitHub's own, for the same reason; gitleaks-action is free for personal accounts.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Pinning actions to SHAs** blocks a moved tag from changing CI, the usual supply-chain hole in GitHub Actions. Updates need a bump: Dependabot for actions comes with TODO 11.5.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Before the CI secret scan, the history was checked for key-like strings** (`sk-ant-…`, `sk-…`, `*_API_KEY=<value>`) and `.env` was confirmed never committed. Nothing was found.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Most of the code sits outside `tsc`'s reach.** The inline module script in `index.html` holds most of the logic and isn't type-checked, only linted. Moving logic out into `src/*.js` modules, as was done for `engine.js`, `store.js`, `prompt.js` and `style.js`, brings it under both checks and unit tests.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-20 — Local dev server and justfile
nodes.annotation: TODO items: none directly; dev tooling that later supports 1.3 and 2.1.

nodes.text: - Local serving moved from `python3 -m http.server` to Node for the `just` recipes, in line with the Node stack. `npm run serve` in `claude/` still uses Python.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Python's `http.server` sends `text/html` without a charset. `claude/dist/index.html` is the bare artifact body with no `<meta charset>`, so Chrome decoded it as Windows-1252 and every `≈`, `…` and `·` came out garbled. `/_test.html` and `codex/` were fine because they declare their charset. Any server we ship should set the charset in the header and not rely on the markup.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Having our own server makes it easy to add COOP/COEP later, which multi-threaded Stockfish needs (TODO 1.3).
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-20 — Milestone 1: play against the engine

nodes.text: - **Draw offers only go one way:** Stockfish never offers a draw itself.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **1.8:** starting from a curriculum position moved to 6.8, because there is no curriculum yet. `newGame` already starts from any FEN or move list.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **No `[%clk]` comments in the PGN**, only the `TimeControl` tag.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Timeout draws use a simplified rule:** a lone king, or a king and one minor piece against a lone king, can't mate. FIDE asks whether any legal sequence mates, which is rarely different in practice.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **1.4 stays open.** Below 1320 the levels are now aligned with Stockfish's UCI_Elo scale. That scale is calibrated against engine rating lists, not human ratings, and the 1320+ levels run at our short think times with the lite network. Tying the slider to human ratings needs results from real players, e.g. from the weakness tracking in 9.2.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **chess.js keeps castling rights without a rook** and then generates O-O-O in `4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K2R w KQkq`. Every pasted FEN now goes through `fixCastling`.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **MultiPV can explode in won positions.** On a mate in one whose alternatives lose, MultiPV 3 at depth 16 took 8 s single-threaded and over 30 s with 4 threads; with MultiPV 1 it takes 0.3 s. The time cap bounds it. On normal positions, 4 threads reach depth 16 about 30–45% faster.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Search depth dominates the weakened mode.** Depth 1 → 3 → 5 changed strength by hundreds of Elo, far more than the "keep the best move" chance. The old table's depth 5 from 1100 up made 1300 stronger than 1320. Calibrate whenever these knobs change: the script takes about 12 minutes.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **chess.js parses NAGs but drops them**, so `pgn.js` re-reads the movetext. Its ply count is tested against chess.js's history so the two can't drift apart.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **The calibration's noise is about ±70 Elo per level** at 120 games. 1100 came out above 1200 in run 3, although 1200 searches at the same depth and keeps the best move more often. More games would narrow this; the ordering is right in expectation.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-20 — One app folder: `site/`

nodes.text: - **No `client`/`server`/`shared` workspaces (TODO 0.3).** One npm project is enough while the client has no build beyond copying files. 0.3 stays open for when that changes.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **The old `codex/` copy and the root `package.json` are left on disk** for the user to delete. The tool's permission rules blocked the deletion, and `site/` replaces both.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - `codex/` never held a separate implementation. Apart from the gateway client added on 2026-10-20, it was `claude/`'s build output, byte for byte. Committing build output as a "variant" made one codebase look like two; a real comparison would need both agents to work from the same task description.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - `codex/index.html` had been saved from the artifact host, so it carried the host's base CSS. The page's own CSS already covers what matters locally (`[hidden]`, `box-sizing`), so the build doesn't need it.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Multi-threaded Stockfish needs `SharedArrayBuffer`, which needs cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP headers). That constrains server headers and any third-party embeds, so it should be settled early (TODO 1.3, 2.1).
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-20 — Stockfish playing style

nodes.text: - **Choice groups wrap on narrow screens.** `.choice` now wraps and draws dividers as 1 px gaps, so five buttons fit a phone. Desktop looks the same as before (`width: fit-content`).
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Style isn't a Stockfish option.** Stockfish 19's UCI options were checked directly: Skill Level, UCI_LimitStrength and UCI_Elo (minimum 1320), with no Contempt or aggressiveness setting. So style is a choice among Stockfish's candidate moves, made after the strength limit.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **The aggression score is a heuristic, not tuned on real games.** It works on the test positions, and Reckless does choose sacrifices. Whether players feel the difference is worth checking during the Elo calibration (TODO 1.4).
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Stockfish already searches several lines when strength-limited.** With `Skill Level` or `UCI_LimitStrength` on, it searches at least 4 lines internally to choose its weaker move. So the move it plays is normally among the reported lines, and asking for 4 costs little extra.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Strength first, then style.** The window is measured from the move Stockfish would play under its Elo limit, not from the best move. So a style changes how Stockfish plays, not how strong it is, and a forced mate is never given up: a mate outranks any centipawn line by far more than any window.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-21 — Answers: wrong moves underlined, game references linked to the game

nodes.text: - **"Links to the original" means the game in our own collection, not an external site.** The link always leads to a game record we've checked with chess.js, and the page never builds a URL from model output. External sources (Wikipedia, a game database) could be added per classic as fixed links later.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Only the 13 built-in classics are recognised.** Games in the player's library or imported studies aren't, because their names (player pairings, events) are too ambiguous to match safely in free text.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **The preview is a cheap version of ROAD's scratch board.** It borrows the board for as long as the pointer stays on the link. A variation stepper (4.3) can grow from the same `previewPosition` and `syncBoard` handover.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **A name only links when it means one game.** "Philidor" alone is also an opening and "Lucena" a person, so they need "position" or "study" after them. For the same reason, "Rubinstein's Immortal" must not also match "Immortal Game".
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-21 — CI: secret scan permissions

nodes.text: - CI ran only on the PR into `main`. The stacked PRs #2–#10 (based on feature branches) never created a workflow run.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-21 — Classic games for the coach: a first collection, retrieved by theme

nodes.text: - **The scores were written from memory.** chess.js can prove every move legal and every final mate real, but not that a game was played exactly so. The collection is small and limited to the most-published games. A larger one needs sources and licences per item (7.1).
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Position matching rarely finds a classic.** An exact position or pawn structure is a strong signal, but too rare to catch most games; tags by theme and opening family find a classic for most positions.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-21 — Explanation modes: commentary, challenges, interesting moves

nodes.text: - **Challenges stay out of games** unless help is Full engine. Asking for the best move or the threat would otherwise hand out engine help the player switched off.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **"Trap" is a heuristic.** It marks a piece offered that the engine's own line doesn't take: what looks free to a human, not proven to lose for whoever takes it.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **The first threat test was wrong.** It judged a threat by how much the opponent's evaluation improves if they could move now. When the side to move has mate in one, every opponent move looks like a huge "threat". A threat has to be concrete: a mate, or material won along the opponent's line.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Evaluations need a side.** "+4.81" for a threat confused even me. Challenge evaluations now always say for whom ("it would give Black +4.70").
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **A trade isn't a sacrifice.** Material has to be counted across the whole exchange: Bxf6 Qxf6 is even, while Nxb5 cxb5 Bxb5+ leaves a knight for two pawns.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-21 — Fix: a rejected request says why; no key fragments in the log
nodes.annotation: TODO items: fix for 2.x (the AI gateway's errors).

nodes.text: - **The same model fails differently depending on the request.** Ollama answers the old model with 404 "not found" through the SDK's streaming request, but with 400 "does not support chat" through a plain one. Both now say what's wrong. The cure is `ollama pull deepseek-r1` again, or another model from `ollama list`.

nodes.text: - **Then the check went wrong.** Once the findings were in the chat's context, the check struck through correct moves: the turning points' better lines (from other positions), and game moves after the position on the board. Context and check have to grow together.

nodes.text: - **The model matters.** With `claude-haiku-5-5`, the default, the answers were thinner and sometimes misleading ("Black's queen is gone" for a queen trade). With Opus, the coach proposed 9… h6 as its own idea, found the catch itself (the queen on f6 no longer guards b7), and said it couldn't evaluate the move. The check marked its untested line "Bxf6 Qxf6" as not one of the engine's.

nodes.title: 2026-10-21 — Offline mode: a small model in the browser
nodes.annotation: TODO items: 2.16.0, 2.16.1, 2.16.3–2.16.6 done; 2.16.2 partly (model choice with the eval set, 3.8).

nodes.text: - **wllama only, not WebLLM first (2.16.1).** wllama has run on WebGPU since v3, with WebAssembly as its own fallback. One MIT dependency with one wasm file covers both paths and loads any GGUF file from our server. WebLLM would need its own compiled model libraries and a second runtime. Chrome's built-in model is still open.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Not in our Worker.** wllama starts its own worker (from a blob URL, allowed by `worker-src blob:`), so the page-side provider doesn't need one.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Model chosen before the eval set exists.** Qwen2.5 is well known, Apache-2.0, has no "thinking" mode to switch off, and has official GGUF files. 3.8 should decide between it and newer small models. Adding one is a catalog entry.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: The answer check (3.4) marks wrong moves either way. A small model is fine for putting the engine's facts into words, not for chess judgement.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **Speed on WebGPU (Apple silicon, Chrome):** a full coach answer to a 2,950-character prompt took about 4 s with the 0.5B model.
nodes.heading: Insights
Insights

nodes.text: - **The browser's storage quota is the real limit, not memory.** wllama always downloads into the browser's private storage (OPFS), even with `useCache: false`. A 1.1 GB model failed in the test browser with "exceed its storage quota", as it would in a private window. The page now checks `navigator.storage.estimate()` first: when the model doesn't fit, or caching fails on the quota, it fetches the file itself and hands it to wllama in memory. The 0.5 GB model fit either way, which is why only the default model showed the problem.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **A test that waits for the "thinking" style to go reads a half-streamed answer.** It disappears with the first chunk; the Stop button only disappears at the end.

nodes.title: 2026-10-21 — Tutor commentary: aspects, templates, checked answers, when to comment, cache

nodes.text: - **Flagged, not dropped (3.4).** Removing text from an answer would change what it says. Marking it and telling the player keeps the coach honest, and the player can still read the rest.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **The review summary isn't checked.** It talks about many positions at once, so a check against one position's lines would mark correct moves. It still gets the shared rules.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **No threat search.** "What's next" uses the engine's top lines and the motif detectors. A separate null-move search for threats is part of the engine tools (4.11).
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **3.2.5 uses the player's library.** The classic games collection (7.3) doesn't exist yet. The Similar games aspect uses the similar positions already retrieved from the player's library and the built-in examples.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - OpenAI and Mistral have no results yet. The OpenAI key in `.env` was refused (401), and Mistral rate-limited every request. Those first runs were scored as if the error messages were answers, which is how we found the error handling was missing. We deleted those reports. Re-run them once the keys work: `just eval openai judge=anthropic`.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - **Haiku misses endgame theory.** It didn't mention the opposition in the king-and-pawn position, and the judge confirmed it. The retrieved classics (3.2.5) include the endgame studies, but no king-and-pawn opposition example yet, so that's where to add one.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **2.16.2:** the 1.5B model stays the default in the browser, being clearly better than 0.5B. It's a fallback for offline and private use, not a substitute for a cloud model. A 3–4B model is worth evaluating once WebGPU memory allows.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text:
- **Key points have to follow the engine, not the textbook.**
  - In the Lucena position, Opus followed Stockfish's line, 1. Rb1 and 2. Rd1+, then the king walks out, and never built the textbook bridge on the fourth rank. Its answer is correct, but it misses that key point.
  - A key point that the engine's line doesn't need measures book knowledge, not coaching. That's why the judge, with Stockfish's lines as the truth, stays part of the score.
  - Matching by regex is cheap but coarse, so each report keeps the judge's notes beside it.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - **The engine grounding works, but explaining is the hard part.** Even the 0.5B model rarely names a wrong move, because it copies Stockfish's lines. What the small models can't do is say *why*, and the judge scores insight lowest.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-23 — Explicit passage embeddings and dense retrieval comparison

nodes.text: - This is a bounded memory-only index over the current source passages. Persistent/server vector stores, larger licensed corpora, hybrid ranking and tutor citation integration remain separate items. The revision is operator-supplied, not independently attested against weights; unknown revisions remain explicit. Ollama installations lacking the required local-model metadata fail closed.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Shared lexical gold is retained for comparability. Its German “Isolani”/English-guide case can have a useful bilingual semantic match despite its no-answer label; the report flags this intent limitation. Semantic label review is needed before using the aggregate false-positive rate to calibrate abstention. Off-topic and unsupported-proof cases still lack supporting passages.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The real-model comparison is an explicit manual evaluation; automated tests only use mock/fake providers. Its small authored development suite is not held-out evidence of generalisation, chess accuracy or answer quality.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Better paraphrase recall can coexist with substantially worse abstention. Positive cosine similarity cannot establish that a permitted passage answers a question; 8.4 needs separate relevance/abstention evaluation before 8.6 feeds retrieved text to the coach.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Configured chat and embedding providers can differ. Reusing chat configuration under local-only mode must not silently substitute credentials/endpoints while retaining another provider's name.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A local service can relay a cloud model. Local-only enforcement needs model-level evidence as well as a provider label, and its policy must be rechecked after asynchronous work.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-23 — Fuzzy pawn-structure distance

nodes.text: - The runtime consumer is Combined Library passage search. The older Reading/coach `similarPositions()` buckets and their original position benchmark remain unchanged; richer position-index work remains 8.1. Material/placement features, richer motif indexing and tutor retrieval/citations remain 8.1/8.2/8.6. No new provider, dependency, external corpus or `llmkit` code was added.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Chose the transparent square-set overlap baseline from the similarity research; the cutoff is an explicit heuristic, not a tuned relevance threshold. A one-square and a distant relocation have the same feature cost, and a missing pawn is cheaper than moving it. Assignment/transport or learned distances need separate definitions, labels and evaluation.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Fuzzy-match intent belongs in the same captured query state as board FEN and literal-term policy. Changing it can invalidate an asynchronous result or held source action without changing the game generation.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Distance zero on pawn features is not board identity, and empty pawn sets need an explicit retrieval eligibility rule. Rights and side still belong to the exact board key.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A graded overlap baseline recovers some useful structural neighbours while visibly missing sparse endings. Keep that failure in the labels rather than choosing a cutoff that hides it or presenting distance as confidence.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-23 — Hybrid passage retrieval with explicit board intent

nodes.text: - Measurements use small authored development sets, not held-out evidence of generalisation or chess/answer quality. The real embedding run is a manual local evaluation; automatic tests use mock/fake providers only. Local-only, model metadata, budgets and source/licence assertions keep their existing semantics.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - This delivers bounded rank fusion and a deterministic reranker over existing chess signals, with no learned cross-encoder or calibrated semantic abstention. Material/piece-placement signatures, richer position/move motif tags and fuzzy pawn distance remain 8.1/8.2/8.5. Tutor prompts and citation validation remain 8.6. No dependency, external corpus or `llmkit` code was added.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A literal all-terms requirement offers predictable empty results at a measurable recall cost. It does not replace semantic support labels or calibrated abstention; unchanged lexical-intent labels also need care when interpreting bilingual semantic matches.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Board relevance is query state, not just game identity. Cursor and scratch changes can occur without a new generation, so both asynchronous completion and held source actions must capture and recheck the intended board.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Fusion cannot repair unsupported evidence by itself and can lose the best individual retriever's paraphrase recall. Keep method ablations and no-answer rates visible rather than promoting an aggregate ranking score as confidence.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A rejected request is not evidence that a model lacks tool support. Capability state must follow the selected model and be based on an explicit capability failure.

nodes.text: - Native tool schemas and runtime instructions serve different purposes: schemas define valid calls, while runtime instructions make the current engine access explicit. These instructions extend the standing rules rather than displacing the first-turn security contract.
