nodes.text: - Returning to the initial diagram later in a line is not a fresh start: capture keeps that move history, while position queries intentionally merge the repeated diagram.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Scratch boards may begin at the current position, an ancestor or an independent standard start. Capturing a repertoire needs an explicit connecting path, rather than concatenating every visible game move with the scratch line.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A position graph is useful for “my chosen moves here”, while the original route is needed to edit and rehearse an opening. Keeping both avoids losing move-order choices at transpositions.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Approved German provider trials and a prose-capture correction
nodes.annotation: TODO items: 10.8.4.2; parent 10.8.4 and follow-up 10.8.4.3 remain open.

nodes.text: - Claude's retained cue score is not a model-only quality score: Lucena's bridge cue, for example, appeared only in a supplied source. The two automatically flagged move tokens include an impossible capture discussed as such and a piece reference; they are not independently verified recommendations to play illegal moves. There was no semantic judge and no paid rerun to conceal the capture problem.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The provider comparison is incomplete: credentials, rate limits and the missing configured Ollama model prevented three providers from answering. Fresh comparable prose-only captures need a new approved plan after those prerequisites are fixed. The parent TODO remains open.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Grounding material is useful context but must not earn credit for the model explaining it. Separating provider failures, observed checker flags, capture versions and semantic assessment makes the experiment reviewable without turning transport success or a lexical match into a coaching-quality claim.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Bounded model downloads verified before publication

nodes.text: - The deadline covers download headers/body, rather than unrelated local preflight hash checks. File/marker publication consists of two atomic replacements; interruption can leave verified weights requiring another full check. Abrupt crashes can leave unserved unique partials; only handled failures/cancellation promise cleanup.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The stored hash marker retains its operator-controlled quick-check contract. It is not a fresh digest of every served byte and does not detect every same-size local edit with an old marker. Remaining logging, file-serving/scanner and release findings are separate.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Rejecting an oversized file after it has filled the disk is too late. Enforcing the byte bound before each write and delaying publication until verification gives the integrity check a resource boundary as well as a final yes/no result.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Combined library metadata search

nodes.text: - Search is over recorded metadata, not automatic motif diagnosis, source prose or model-inferred history. Structured fields and search words are page-local rather than persisted preferences. Imported games without tags remain searchable by their other fields; position/move pattern indexing remains TODO 8.2.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Updating catalogue labels must not replace unrelated source editing controls. Retaining unchanged record cards keeps unsaved corrections and keyboard focus through asynchronous data readiness.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Display, browse and coach search need the same date/result/opening facts. Legal PGN-derived labels avoid dependence on whether the opening catalogue happened to arrive before import, while explicit unknown years prevent false historical matches.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Compare position retrieval with literature algorithms
nodes.annotation: TODO items: documentation follow-up to completed 8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 8.5 and 8.8; no new algorithm milestone completed.

nodes.text: - This is a sourced algorithm comparison and experiment design, not a reproduction of literature algorithms on Kibitz's corpus. Published metrics with different inputs, labels and denominators are not combined into a performance ranking.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Similarity of pawn squares, source occurrences, explanation passages and tactical solutions are different retrieval objectives. The relevant literature comparison depends on which one the query requests.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Conservative PGN import deduplication

nodes.text: - Deduplication matches conservative source documents rather than fuzzy game identity. Differently annotated/headered/licensed versions can remain separate even with the same moves, and built-ins are outside the user's import scope. Existing duplicates are not deleted. Account matching uses the current client snapshot plus its acknowledged imports; a future server uniqueness transaction is needed for simultaneous devices.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A successful account write can precede its subscription snapshot. Remembering acknowledgements is necessary for retry-safe deduplication, while counting only records visible in the UI would create new IDs during that gap. Duplicate-only imports must avoid writing so that quota failures cannot turn a harmless repeat into an apparent failed save.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A mainline-only hash would silently discard distinct annotations, variations and attribution. The original PGN must remain the evidence document; normalization only belongs in a derived comparison key.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Curriculum records and Lessons catalogue

nodes.text: - This completes the records and catalogue in 6.1. Expanded tactics/strategy/endgames, puzzle ingestion, the interactive lesson player, grading, progress and play-out remain separately tracked in 6.2–6.8. Prerequisites describe a learning sequence; no progress lock is imposed before 6.7 exists.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Legal replay, proved terminal mate and an authored reflection rubric are different evidence classes. Keeping the exercise goal explicit avoids treating every recorded move as a unique engine-approved answer.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Browser consumers of pure modules must update together, and translated teaching text should bypass the interface translator. Catalogue filters belong to their panel rather than the active board or global coach state.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Endgame lessons with recorded Syzygy evidence

nodes.text: - Evidence is bundled for fixed teaching diagrams rather than fetching arbitrary player positions at runtime. This completes the authored endgame catalogue and its tablebase checks; interactive play and alternative-answer grading remain 6.6. A checked branch preserves the result, but does not claim a unique best move or force the opponent to follow that branch. Conventional diagrams do not resolve the separately tracked historical publication/licensing work in 7.3/7.4.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The same opposition placement is drawn with White to move and winning for White with Black to move. Reading the latter API `loss` as a White loss would reverse the lesson; a child move’s category needs the opposite turn again.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - EPD is suitable for the project’s engine cache, but full FEN is required for this evidence: fifty-move counters can change tablebase results. Missing evidence for a changed counter fails closed instead of borrowing a nearby snapshot.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Exclude agent instructions from aggregate PDFs
nodes.annotation: TODO items: none; requested documentation tooling maintenance.

nodes.text: - No application changes or new dependencies; no TODO milestone applies.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Aggregate document generation can skip agent instructions without disabling explicit single-document conversion.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Explicit provider/purpose opt-in and privacy notice

nodes.text: - Per-purpose controls are narrower than a single provider toggle. Mock mode and the browser model do not need a network-provider permission; browser model loading retains its existing resource consent. Host-managed artifacts keep their separate host contract.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Consent headers attest a local operator/browser choice and provide routing/version preconditions; they are not authentication or legal consent receipts. Revocation cannot recall transmitted data or stop all provider-side work already accepted. Truly simultaneous localStorage writers lack a transaction; failed revocations warn about other tabs/reloads until saved. No provider-retention/compliance guarantee is invented.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A connection test also contacts a provider and needs consent. Embedding ingestion has a different data scope from coach context, so sharing a provider name is insufficient permission to send passages or queries.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Freshly checked exercises from own-game mistakes

nodes.text: - Exercises target current engine move quality and accept alternatives; they do not claim forced wins, calibrated difficulty, flawless endgame grading or learner mastery. Help/reveal/rules-mate/engine-target remain distinct. Durable practice scheduling remains 9.4. No model request, new dependency, source upload or persistent schema migration is introduced.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Independent boards need keyboard and asynchronous boundaries as well as separate chess objects. Guarding only mouse moves would still let focused practice controls alter the main board or receive late results from another context.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A historical classification is a candidate source, not a current solution. Rechecking both the reference and the player's original move avoids generating an obsolete exercise; grading other legal answers avoids confusing a bounded reference with a unique good move.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — German opening labels and authored classic-game notes

nodes.text: - The first full browser run had 364 passes and one initial offline-install assertion timeout. Its 20-second assertion was shorter than the app's existing 120-second installation deadline; the corrected wait passed all seven focused offline cases and the entire subsequent 365-case run. The final dependency update changes build/test handling, with identical generated app bytes as described above.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - German lexical/source-navigation tests do not claim a new retrieval-quality score or prove translated prose/chess claims. The existing frozen English benchmark and canonical chess data remain separate.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A translated annotated PGN is a different source document even when every chess move is unchanged. Its hashes and citation offsets must be generated from the actual language-specific text.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Isolated lesson player and authored tutor hints

nodes.text: - Tutor hints and explanations are authored and available offline. Source-line recall and reflection self-assessment are labelled as such; no model-generated correctness grade, fresh strength verdict for arbitrary alternatives or measured learning gain is claimed. Persistence and per-theme aggregation remain 6.7; playing a lesson against Stockfish remains 6.8.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Session identity alone does not reject a held navigation button after a worked-view cursor change. A render version guards those controls too, and promotion callbacks additionally require their original dialog. Manual localization must cover attributes as well as text nodes to avoid duplicate translation.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A rules-proven mate, recall of a source solution and an authored reflection rubric are different evidence classes. Separate completion kinds let later progress summaries preserve those distinctions rather than count every interaction as mastered chess.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Keyboard board play, patterned marks and reduced motion

nodes.text: - [Controls and verification limits](ACCESSIBILITY.md) document Chrome automation/visual inspection and the remaining need for hands-on assistive-technology testing; no WCAG conformance claim is made.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Existing typed SAN/UCI input and independent lesson/drill/own-mistake controls remain available. The new square grid targets the main board and free scratch board rather than replacing every practice widget.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A CSS reduced-motion rule does not stop a JavaScript board animator. Keyboard selection also needs to clear the pointer renderer's previous origin before selecting another piece.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Lichess puzzle source and offline import pipeline

nodes.text: - Bundled a documented starter prefix rather than the entire multi-million-puzzle database. It demonstrates ingestion and source-aware catalogue use, not representative theme coverage, calibrated teaching difficulty or measured learning benefit. Lichess rating bands are editorial navigation, not playing Elo. Interactive solving, hints and alternative-answer grading remain 6.6. Local legality/mate checks do not independently verify other source strength or theme claims.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Lichess’s first UCI move belongs to the opponent. Showing the raw database FEN would present the wrong side and task; applying the setup move is a data-model invariant rather than a UI convention.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Source IDs use both cases. Lowercasing them would merge distinct puzzles; encoding each character preserves identity within the curriculum’s existing ID alphabet. Keeping the original CSV also makes generated records auditable when the live export later changes.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Literal phrase interpolation and anchored opening families
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.2.4; source fixes for CodeQL contexts 16/17 under [#99](https://github.com/gregoryyy/kibitz/issues/99), which remains open for other findings and scanner verification.

nodes.text: - These changes fix two source bugs rather than resolving all of #99. Other scanner contexts, file races and post-merge main-branch scan evidence remain open. No alerts are dismissed and the release gate remains incomplete.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A replacement-string API interprets dollar sequences even when the surrounding pattern is a literal star. A callback inserts the value unchanged and does not recursively expand stars inside it.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Phrase interpolation returns plain text. Fixing all slots addresses its semantics; it does not make the helper an HTML sanitizer or establish a cross-site scripting exploit in the original code.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Local application threat model

nodes.text: - This completes the threat-model item rather than the separate OWASP/ASVS/scanning/release gates. Existing code-scanning alerts, model/file handling, log privacy and resource-bound review remain explicit follow-ups under 11.2–11.6/12.3. Cookie grouping and provider consent attestations are not described as hosted authentication.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A legal move, a source hash, a permitted endpoint and a successful feature test establish different facts. Keeping these boundaries explicit prevents a citation or a local deployment label from implying stronger guarantees than the implementation provides.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Local spaced practice across lessons, openings and own mistakes

nodes.text: - Reused the project's existing deterministic interval heuristic rather than introducing a fitted memory model or dependency. No old lesson totals are retrospectively assigned invented intervals. Schedules remain browser-local and owner-scoped rather than synchronized with a selected server library.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Lesson counters and scheduling are separate acknowledged keys, not a cross-key transaction. Closing/reloading loses unsaved in-tab receipts; bounded retry IDs do not promise indefinite deduplication. Simultaneous localStorage writers still lack a transaction. [Practice lifecycle](PRACTICE.md) records these limits, date assumptions, caps and revision retention.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A due queue can share timing without conflating what each activity establishes. Keeping self-assessment, recall, engine evidence and rules mate visible is necessary before later personalization can interpret the records.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Material and piece-placement position indexes

nodes.text: - This milestone supplies the missing position features and typed lookup API. Default Reading/Combined ranking remains unchanged; no similarity weights, learned metric, new UI controls or retrieval-quality improvement are claimed. Geometry checks validate encoding, while source compilation supplies rules validation. No database schema or stored library record is migrated.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Derived feature additions need not invalidate a frozen source benchmark. Replaying both recorded baselines demonstrates that this index extension leaves the existing measured retrieval behavior intact.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Equal scalar piece value loses piece-class information; equal placement loses side to move, rights and counters. Explicit keys and match reasons preserve these different meanings without conflating a structural analogy with an exact game state or objective chess evidence.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Native TLS protection for newly issued usage cookies
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.2.6; cookie transport context 4 under [#99](https://github.com/gregoryyy/kibitz/issues/99).

nodes.text: - Context 4 is handled according to the selected local deployment. Native TLS issuance is fixed; supported loopback HTTP intentionally remains clear-text transport. The historical scanner alert is not dismissed and broader #99/scanner/release gates remain open.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Reusing a valid cookie preserves its original browser attributes; a policy/transport migration must clear old cookies rather than claim that a response silently upgraded them.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A forwarded scheme header describes a claim, while the native socket describes this connection. Using only the latter keeps cookie issuance consistent with the library's existing policy.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Optional Chrome built-in coach
nodes.annotation: TODO items: remaining 2.16.1 Chrome runtime; 2.16 completed with documented runtime differences.

nodes.text: - Chrome manages its model outside Kibitz's pinned catalogue and public offline cache, and its current API is unavailable in Workers. These explicit optional-runtime exceptions replace the earlier unimplemented Chrome note; they do not change wllama's deployment guarantees. Model availability/resource admission belongs to Chrome; character/time limits do not pretend to measure native tokens.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Synchronous creation failures need the same settled-load cleanup as rejected promises, and input limits must include separators inserted while merging turns. Both boundaries have regression assertions.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Remembering a backend is different from authorizing a model download. A fresh disposable context per request also prevents browser-maintained history from bypassing the application's own context controls.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Optional German move letters and figurines

nodes.text: - The first full browser run had 360 passes and one pre-existing scratch-board assertion failure before a move. That case passed five unchanged repeats, and the subsequent complete run passed all 361 cases. No product change or assertion relaxation was made for that intermittent failure.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Display formatting recognizes actual SAN tokens; it does not rewrite arbitrary imported or model prose. English SAN stays the default independently of interface language.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Display notation needs to remain separate from canonical move data, especially when repainting an answer or switching interface language. A figurine's visible glyph also needs an accessible move description.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Optional SQLite library and scoped browser cache

nodes.text: - SQLite stores original game/reference documents; source/position/passage indexes remain derived in-memory data. IndexedDB is the optional server library's cache, while the default browser collection remains in localStorage. No legacy migration, automatic library merge, offline write queue or authenticated account service is introduced. Anonymous cookie ownership supports the local-server workflow; deployment/accounts remain 10.1–10.2, full offline loading remains 10.7.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A durable server commit and a browser-cache transaction have different outcomes. Treating the latter as the save result would falsely report failure after a successful commit, inviting unnecessary duplicates. Explicit refresh and conservative import matching resolve uncertain receipts without blind overwrites.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - An origin-local cache does not establish the current cookie owner. Verification must precede cached fallback after a fresh load, and changes of storage context must invalidate queued work and held controls as well as visible indexes.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Organize source modules by responsibility

nodes.text: - The requested scope is the organization of existing JavaScript modules. The page still composes them through its inline application module, preserving the artifact and local-page formats.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Removing old build assets makes missing path migrations visible instead of allowing stale flat files to satisfy imports.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A source move reaches more than browser imports: the gateway and offline benchmarks consume the same pure modules, and JSDoc imports need the same path updates.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — OWASP Top 10 code mapping and tracked findings

nodes.text: - Findings are tracked rather than presented as fixed. Seven scanner-rated high alerts remain unresolved alongside the other findings. The LLM Top 10, ASVS, automated-scan/baseline and release gates remain open; this checklist is not an exhaustive new browser audit or an all-clear release result.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A security checklist needs a disposition for each observation, including local-only assumptions and queries over trusted HTML/test fixtures. Mapping an alert to its actual sink and recording a synthetic reproduction gives the next fix a testable target without confusing a scanner label with demonstrated impact.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Persistent local AI usage and per-browser request limits
nodes.annotation: TODO items: 2.11, scoped by the selected local single-user deployment (10.1).

nodes.text: - Hosted accounts and authenticated quotas remain deferred with 10.2, as selected by the owner. Cookie replacement can restart an individual scope; aggregate server counters remain independent. The browser model does not pass through this gateway ledger.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Budgets are admission thresholds on completed reported usage, not reservations or hard billing caps. Final/in-flight calls, provider retries/fallbacks and crashes before usage recording can exceed or under-report them; provider-side spending caps remain necessary for hard financial limits. Operational counter retention/reset is separate from chess-data erasure and explicitly disclosed.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Durable cookie counters require a shared transactional store, but do not create authentication. Route/consent/payment classification must also be captured at the same point after asynchronous request-body reads.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Play lesson positions against Stockfish

nodes.text: - The current game keeps running while confirmation or saving is pending. A changed position/state prevents replacement and asks the player to start again; a previously authorized detached snapshot may already have saved. This preserves running-game behavior without pausing/resuming clocks around a separate lesson board. Practice games use ordinary game progress/review rather than being graded as lesson solutions.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A lesson's displayed worked position can differ from both its initial diagram and the attempted solution. The explicit handoff must capture that full FEN and validate that it remains playable. A theoretical tablebase draw is still a useful practice position; a rules-ended game is not.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Cancelling a dialog does not cancel a storage write already in flight. Serializing subsequent handoffs and checking both the lesson and main-game context after the write prevents an older request from replacing a newly selected game.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Player profile and reported rating context

nodes.text: - This is a browser-local profile, without account synchronization or automatic performance-derived ability estimation. A reported rating is optional context, independent of explanation level and playing strength. Weakness tracking, own-mistake tasks and scheduling remain 9.2–9.4; broader export/deletion remains 10.3.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Draft fields and effective preferences need separate lifetimes. A storage event can update current coaching context while preserving typed input, but that draft must not silently overwrite a newer profile—even through an unrelated level click.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Explanation style, a rating from a particular pool/time control, and opponent strength are different settings. Removing implied rating bands avoids contradictory teaching context when a player deliberately chooses simpler or deeper explanations.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Prepare German tutor evaluation and explicit live-run plan
nodes.annotation: TODO items: 10.8.4.1; live provider matrix 10.8.4.2 remains open.

nodes.text: - The [live-run plan](eval/german-plan.md) records model IDs and pending trials separately. No provider result is fabricated from a mock run, English report, configured key or failed connection. The existing paid-run approval requirement remains in effect; 10.8.4 is not marked complete before live trials are recorded.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Regex cues can match negations and irrelevant mentions. A test explicitly records this limit; translated patterns do not establish semantic correctness or calibrated cross-language rankings. Printed position counts are not hard request/cost caps when agent follow-ups and rate-limit retries occur.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Language-specific quick-question labels and load-success messages belong to the actual UI path. A valid German benchmark must preserve chess positions/concepts while retaining the language and source text used for every reported cue score.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Private databases excluded from every served root

nodes.text: - A missing explicit model directory is rejected instead of treating it as an empty served tree. This prevents ambiguous future paths from bypassing database validation. Static/model file-descriptor races, model trust, download bounds and default logging remain separate findings; this does not complete the release gate.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A “private file outside the web root” check must know every tree the process can serve. Resolving public roots before private storage initialization makes that contract testable even when a second route has a strict filename allowlist.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Private runtime logs and local operator monitoring

nodes.text: - Monitoring targets the selected local single-user deployment: operator status/event inspection, without an external service or user-identifying audit trail. No verbose payload mode was added. Runtime/OS warnings and operator capture utilities have separate output; static-file race/error paths remain under #99.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Historical main-branch CodeQL alert 18 is not dismissed by a feature PR. It requires post-merge scan evidence; broader LLM/ASVS/scanner/release gates remain open.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Removing recognized keys from SDK prose does not remove personal data reflected by a provider. Closed-vocabulary fields avoid depending on an incomplete secret detector.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A streamed HTTP 200 can carry a failed answer. Monitoring needs the bounded AI error event as well as the access status, while a cancelled request can be described without recording who made it.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Published classic-game sources and expanded collection

nodes.text: - The collection records published versions actually checked, with fixed revision/page references. It does not claim to authenticate every first historical publication; disputed teaching versions stay labelled. The two incomplete book scores are not completed from memory or mixed with another source. Study-source verification remains the separate 7.4 milestone. Public-domain status is recorded as supplied for the USA, without a blanket worldwide assertion.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The retrieval benchmark remains a fixed development corpus; this addition makes no new retrieval-quality or learner-outcome claim about the larger production library. Its earlier metadata remains in the snapshot for reproducibility.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Legal replay alone cannot establish historical provenance. Published scores can omit moves, normalize dates or include a later demonstration after resignation. Binding source versions and showing these distinctions prevents a valid chess line from becoming a false historical claim.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A growing production catalogue must not silently alter measured evaluation corpora. Freezing the original records preserves published hashes and comparisons while letting current source metadata and teaching material improve.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Refresh the flipbook with current study flows and fresh coaching
nodes.annotation: TODO items: 12.4.1; broader 12.4 user/provider/Ollama documentation remains open.

nodes.text: - The refresh covers the agreed nineteen-step tour. It does not add an unapproved model benchmark or replace the Primer paper's existing example evidence.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Used the approved Haiku 5.5 routes rather than carrying forward the original Opus snapshot's label or replaying its answers. Mock previews remain outside the published directory; no additional paid rerun was used for visual review or tests.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A valid screenshot can still crop the board. Explicit top framing, focused panel captures and recorded image dimensions make the walkthrough readable and reviewable.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Capturing actual coach prose separately from interface/source cards matters for trustworthy quotations. A complete capture still preserves fallible prose: the graph narration describes a queen/pawn-move pattern even though its listed mistakes include bishop/knight moves. Token checks cannot certify that generalization.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Retrieved coach passages and exact source citations

nodes.text: - This is bounded automatic local retrieval at existing coach request boundaries. Model-requested passage tools, dense/fuzzy tutor retrieval, semantic entailment/abstention checks and outcome evaluation remain future extensions. Library search controls do not silently configure coach lookup. No new provider, dependency, external corpus, gateway route or `llmkit` code was added.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The source bundle belongs in the cache key and the async policy fence. Correct move numbers alone cannot protect a cached answer or a pending source action after account/revision/help changes.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A historical EPD can match twice while its full FEN counters and occurrence differ. Preserve the original occurrence through both retrieval and the final legal replay.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Valid citation identity establishes which supplied source can open, not whether a claim is supported or a source's advice transfers. Source moves must never be added to Stockfish evidence just because they have a citation.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Review-derived phase trends and checked opportunities

nodes.text: - Tracking describes recorded engine decisions/opportunities and heuristic phases, without diagnosing a learner's thought process, estimating ability or proving every possible tactic. Checks cover a bounded subset; unverified is not absence. Old reviews need fresh compatible evidence, and unknown future formats remain preserved. Own-mistake exercises/scheduling remain 9.3–9.4. [Evidence and lifecycle](REVIEWS.md) explain the limits.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A global additive counter would double-count re-reviews and retain deleted/other-context contributions. Source-bound reports aggregated from the current library preserve replacement, deletion and ownership behavior without a second synchronization path.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Reusing source classifications or prose would turn imported claims into measured weaknesses. Capturing fresh qualified analysis and keeping its coverage separate prevents legacy depth-zero values and unsupported motifs from receiving credit.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Saved lesson and theme progress

nodes.text: - Results are local to the browser, with no server synchronization, new provider request or automatic skill estimate. Counts cover completed/revealed exercises, not an unfinished board or written draft. Pending failed saves remain in the current tab and need retry before it closes/reloads. localStorage's single-key write is atomic; simultaneous multi-tab read/modify/write operations are not database transactions. Profile/server storage work remains separately tracked.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Re-rendering the whole catalogue after a save would detach the exercise button used for return focus. Updating badges in place preserves keyboard flow and filter/detail state. Task revisions must include the learning question/rubric as well as the move line, and account for JSON escaping when enforcing bounds.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A completed interaction can be a checked mate, source recall, rubric self-report or revealed example. Tracking those classes separately makes useful practice visible without calling every completion mastery.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Select the local single-user deployment
nodes.annotation: TODO items: 10.1; 2.9's existing env-key path resolved by this decision. Hosted 10.2 deferred.

nodes.text: - This milestone records a deployment decision rather than adding an authentication implementation. The current loopback default already supports the chosen operation. Hosted key/account work is deferred explicitly instead of being presented as completed.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Local hosting and local model inference are independent choices; privacy controls still need to cover an operator-selected cloud model.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Source position themes and recorded move patterns

nodes.text: - Tags reuse existing detectors and describe their current coverage; a missing tag is not proof of absence. No automatic engine sweep, learned ranking, metadata-theme merge, persistent schema migration or new provider/dependency is introduced. Engine-confirmed tactical payoff remains the separate bounded tool verifier. The new source phase context deliberately leaves the recorded hybrid policy intact.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Position identity alone cannot hold context-sensitive facts such as source phase. Occurrence-bound tags preserve these differences, while source revision and ownership guards keep old controls from opening replaced or unrelated records.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A legal source move and a recognized geometric combination are insufficient evidence that a tactic works. Keeping candidate status alongside its exact branch makes that distinction inspectable and testable, even when the next recorded move refutes the motif.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Sourced problems and checked study branches

nodes.text: - This is a curated starter collection of endgame tasks, reusing checked authored material alongside the two published studies and two conventional variants. It does not claim a complete problem corpus or a proof tree over every defence. The Library exposes worked-line inspection on its normal analysis board; interactive lesson solving/progress remains the separate lesson player. No source-view completion is converted into mastery or a performance grade.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A named conventional position need not be the original published diagram. Recording authored variants and their method references avoids borrowing a historical date or a source's licence for a different setup. Shared curriculum examples also need stable lineage rather than duplicated, independently drifting solutions.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Equal piece placement is insufficient for result evidence: side to move and counters can change the outcome. Matching an imported ID is also insufficient for source trust. The exact document/source/branch binding keeps objective chess facts separate from imported claims and prose.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Standalone data exports and confirmed browser/server erasure

nodes.text: - The selected local single-user target uses browser and optional cookie-owned Node storage. Host-managed artifact account libraries, provider retention and operator backups remain outside these controls and are identified explicitly. No hosted-account deletion or forensic disk erasure is claimed.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Browser key removal is not a transaction. Other tabs can recreate in-memory copies, so the page asks the player to close them; partial failure stays visible. Exports preserve saved raw values without adding an import/restore workflow.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Deletion needs both a persistence boundary and an acknowledgement boundary: stopping autosave prevents local recreation, while a retained server revision blocks older writes and keeps uncertain receipts from becoming false success messages.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Strategy lessons and checked structural examples

nodes.text: - This completes authored strategy material for the catalogue. Interactive solving/grading remains 6.6; expert review and measured difficulty/learning outcomes are not claimed. Structural labels and legal candidate demonstrations do not replace current-position engine checks.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A preventive pawn move can create a flight square without answering an immediate threat or being the best move. Explicit rubrics keep a useful observation separate from an unjustified recommendation.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Pawn safety is narrower than piece safety: a pawn-supported square can still be exchanged by a knight. The example teaches both relationships together.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Tactical concept lessons and defensive counterexample

nodes.text: - This completes authored tactical material for catalogue use. Interactive solving and grading remain 6.6. Recorded branches and geometric recognition are explicitly separated from engine-confirmed tactical strength; no empirical difficulty or learner-benefit claim is made.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The same legal branch can illustrate deflection and overloading. Explicit objectives and rubrics explain the relationship without treating either label as a new proof of strength.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A legal refuting capture is a useful teaching example: a fork can be correctly recognized while the move loses its knight. A motif label must not serve as a correctness grade.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Validate and serve one open static/model file
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.2.5; file-serving contexts 7/8 under [#99](https://github.com/gregoryyy/kibitz/issues/99), which remains open for other contexts and main-branch scanner verification.

nodes.text: - The HTTP server now refuses internal asset aliases as well as escaping ones, matching the built offline bundle's regular-file policy. Operator-selected root aliases still work. The implementation is not a filesystem sandbox against an operator changing parent directories or content in place.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - File-serving bugs are fixed without dismissing historical CodeQL alerts. Other #99 contexts and LLM/ASVS/scanner/release gates remain open.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Checking a path and later reopening it lets two operations observe different files. Owning one validated descriptor also gives a clear lifetime to close on every response/error path; bounded streams prevent a late append from exceeding the advertised length.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A catalogue filename alone does not keep bytes inside a model root. A deterministic old-server probe serves a synthetic private file through such a symlink.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-24 — Verified offline app bundle and browser-coach fallback

nodes.text: - Installation controls and quotas are browser dependent. Tests use actual Stockfish but fake browser-model inference; no real-model performance or cross-browser guarantee is inferred. Unknown cached-file loss can require the browser's worker/cache controls if the app page itself cannot load.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - [Offline scope and limits](OFFLINE.md) distinguish a browser-only offline app from locally running Ollama, which still needs the Node gateway. Browser weights need their separate prior load/cache; in-memory fallback is not proof of durable weight storage. Fresh offline private-server collections remain inaccessible without owner verification, while the separate browser library and bundled references work locally.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Re-registering identical worker code does not reconstruct an evicted cache. Cache reads also need to avoid `caches.open()` after erasure, since it creates a new empty cache even from a still-controlled old tab.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Backend-issued local operator sessions (experimental)
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.3 / ASVS 7.2.1. Session termination, explicit function permissions and authenticated client cleanup retain their own final-release gates.

nodes.text: - Local single-user only; no hosted account system, production certificates, real provider calls, new dependency or model download. Operator filesystem ownership remains trusted. Logout/revocation/concurrent termination, permission policy, client-memory/offline cleanup and actual endpoint trust/inventory remain open. The registry retains expired recovery records and refuses new issuance at its bound rather than silently dropping collection ownership; lifecycle cleanup belongs to the next milestone.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Cookie syntax and a private storage scope are not proof of an issued session. Conversely, deleting every old locator when adding authentication loses collection continuity after expiry. Keeping non-authorizing locators and requiring fresh operator proof separates recovery from authorization without rewriting existing private data.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Backend logout and session termination (experimental)
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.4 / ASVS 7.4.1. Explicit function permissions and complete authenticated client-data lifecycle remain separate final-release gates.

nodes.text: - Local single-user only, generated identities/fake providers only, no new dependency or paid inference. Complete DOM/memory/storage/cache/offline cleanup and multi-tab lifecycle remain TODO 11.4.2.11; explicit function permissions remain .5. Already accepted provider work may incur usage after cancellation. Current client refresh/disconnect is not advertised as complete erasure.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Closing a browser cookie is insufficient, and cancelling transport alone cannot prevent a provider that ignores cancellation from returning late data. Durable token removal plus guarded output/mutation boundaries address those separately. Keeping collection locators and ownership bindings avoids turning logout/expiry into accidental data loss.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Bound and privately stage provider fixture recording
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.2.8; capture context 9 under [#99](https://github.com/gregoryyy/kibitz/issues/99). Real missing-provider recordings (2.15) remain open.

nodes.text: - This remediates actual recorder defects and reviews the intended network-to-JSON data flow; it does not manually dismiss or suppress CodeQL context 9. Unknown secrets/encodings, provider semantics and operator-controlled filesystem writers are outside the automatic checks. Main-branch scans, other #99 findings and release approval remain open.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Capture no longer overwrites tracked fixtures by default. Operators review staged responses for private fields before deliberately copying accepted wire data into the repository. An error stops subsequent cases/providers; earlier successful files remain because publication is per file. Abrupt termination can leave a private partial for operator cleanup.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A network-to-file alert can point to intended test-data capture and still reveal real implementation defects. Fixed filenames alone do not protect an existing symlink target or prevent a reflected error response from replacing a useful fixture.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - SDK `logger: null` falls back to console in both installed SDKs. Explicit sinks are needed to keep operator-inherited debug settings out of a capture command's diagnostics.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Confidence-weighted assurance links and review findings

nodes.text: - The first rules infer evidence gaps and review scope. An absent authored `implements`/`verifies` assessment does not prove absent code/tests; a possible deviation impact is not an observed defect or root cause. Negative findings are scoped to the extracted graph and chosen threshold, with limits reported.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Weights are transparent initial support conventions, not calibrated probabilities. No LLM or paid service assigns confidence. Combined reflection headings remain separate from recorded deviations unless an analyst explicitly supplies a typed hypothesis.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Missing traceability and recorded deviations are different observations. Keeping their evidence paths and qualifications visible makes later inference reviewable without converting documentation omissions into defect claims.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Confidence belongs to a relation type: the same artifact pair may support both a strong reference link and a weaker implementation interpretation. Repeating evidence must not inflate support, and filtering must use the effective per-type override rather than retaining the stronger original in parallel.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Encrypted provider, embedding and model-provisioning connections (experimental)
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.7 / ASVS 12.2.1. The reviewed implementation, source-pinned packaged image and updated assessment verify this control; actual endpoint inventory and public trust remain separate.

nodes.text: - Final operator/browser/provider/CDN negotiation and public certificate/renewal evidence remain 11.4.2.6/11.4.2.8. Browser-managed model provisioning is outside the gateway's controls; no inference, model download, production credential/certificate generation or trust installation occurs. Development/recovery remain outside final scope. Existing private data and provider configuration files are not rewritten; an insecure configured provider becomes unavailable until corrected.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - HTTPS on the application listener does not encrypt a second provider hop. Local-only routing, endpoint allowlisting, sharing consent and authenticated function authority are separate decisions from transport encryption. Redirect checks must precede the redirected socket, because validation of only the initial URL leaves download and SDK request paths able to downgrade.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Explicit local operator function permissions (experimental)
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.5 / ASVS 8.2.1. Hosted accounts stay deferred and complete authenticated client-data cleanup remains 11.4.2.11.

nodes.text: - Local operator-owned policy files only; no hosted roles, browser grant editing, new dependency, paid inference or production-key generation. Explicit synthetic HTTP development stays outside final scope. Public assets/client-only operations are outside backend authorization. Already accepted/emitted work cannot be recalled; current permission checks do not claim retroactive erasure of exports or complete offline client cleanup.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Authentication and provider sharing consent do not establish function authority. A separate private allowlist also permits read-only use without granting inference or erasure. Denial must remain distinct from ordinary service downtime, because generic offline fallback could otherwise reopen a cached private collection after an explicit authorization failure.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — GPT-6 Luna Chat Completions tool mode
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 2.10.1. Provider setup documentation remains a separate milestone.

nodes.text: - The provider policy is synthetic and based on the documented contract. This is not a recorded live OpenAI rejection/success, availability check, or benchmark of explanation quality. TODO 2.15 and the missing live-provider comparison evidence remain open.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The correction retains the configured model and Chat Completions transport. It does not add a general reasoning setting or infer compatible model aliases.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A model default can conflict with a tool protocol even when a plain reply works. Connection checks and follow-up turns need the same model-specific transport policy, and the actual per-task selection must take precedence over the configured chat default.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — HTML-aware CSP script selection

nodes.text: - Static serving now requires the installed parser dependency, including without the optional gateway. The CLI gives a bounded actionable startup error if it is missing. Operator-owned public files remain the trust boundary; parsing is not a sanitizer or a release approval.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Incorporated the owner's latest merged main changes into the remaining PR chain without rewriting history, preserving the PDF exclusion and retrieval comparison. Other security/scanner/release items remain open.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Matching `data-src` as though it were `src`, or reading a quoted angle as the tag boundary, can also block valid authored scripts. Browser execution and policy-violation checks distinguish those functional defects from a generic scanner label.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A commented script example can accidentally receive an executable hash when extraction uses a tag regex. Parsing inert content prevents an attacker from reusing that hash for a later inline script, while actual allowed scripts retain their exact normalized text.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Independent provider operation deadlines and response bounds
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.3.10.1; completes the reviewed local resource controls in 11.3.10. Parent 11.3 remains open for model identity and unrestricted claim verification.

nodes.text: - Gateway-created SDK clients no longer retry transient errors automatically; callers see a failure sooner and can deliberately retry. Format/tool/server-side fallbacks can still add calls and total time. Already accepted provider work may continue or be billed after abort, and incomplete usage can remain unreported. These controls are not hard financial caps.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - JavaScript cannot preempt a synchronous parser mid-instruction; bytes bound its input, and the deadline is checked before accepting its result. The SDK's own JSON timer can win the race, so tests verify the stable mapped timeout rather than require one internal error class. The settled full verification was repeated after an earlier build/test overlap; final source/build checks have no intervening rebuild.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Limiting only visible text misses oversized SSE framing, tool arguments and error bodies. Limiting only wire bytes can still admit a very large paragraph into browser rendering; the decoded coaching cap addresses that separate boundary.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - SDK request/header timeouts do not establish a total streamed-body deadline. Actual loopback and old-server regressions distinguish that failure from a synthetic timer-only assertion.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A caller's abort signal and a provider operation's lifetime are related but distinct. Per-call state avoids cancellation/counter interference between concurrent requests and keeps late results from escaping cleanup.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Isolated application HSTS
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.2 / ASVS 3.4.1. Native implementation and actual packaged verification are complete at source `42e6ecd5761f012d9f89c15c8386113e9a01124d`; current-head CI remains recorded in the PR. The other ten ASVS remediations and final-release gate remain open.

nodes.text: - Local resolver mapping and supplied, normally trusted exact-SAN identities are explicit deployment prerequisites. Tests use temporary synthetic certificates and HSTS-enabled curl; actual operator endpoint/TLS/public-trust inventories remain TODO 11.4.2.6/11.4.2.8. Controlled HTTP development and legacy-origin recovery remain outside supported final deployment. Cross-host cookie/usage identities are not silently transferred, and the old groups remain available with their original profile/current database.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - No new npm dependency, provider call, model download, runtime trust bypass, unrelated localhost-wide policy or RC finding dismissal. Cookie backend verification, termination and permissions remain separate work.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - An emitted header is insufficient evidence for a working browser policy: Chromium's localhost exception rules out an apparently convenient hostname. HSTS and cookies also span ports, so isolation belongs to the hostname; comparing Host's published port to the container's internal listener would break valid mappings while adding no authentication.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Keep CodeQL action updates together

nodes.text: - This repairs the existing dependency PR rather than opening another overlapping action upgrade. PR #131's separate initialization bump becomes redundant once #130 merges. No check is suppressed and no application behavior is changed by the action update.
nodes.heading: Deviations and insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Keep provider rejection prose out of public errors
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.3.2.1; completes the reviewed local controls in 11.3.2. Parent 11.3 remains open for model identity, unrestricted misinformation and runtime-stream consumption.

nodes.text: - Public rejection details are deliberately fixed hints. A provider's arbitrary diagnostic prose, model ID, URL or reflected user text is no longer forwarded for display; unknown cases ask the operator to check model/request settings. This does not filter arbitrary generated answers or certify upstream confidentiality. Existing retries/JSON fallbacks are unchanged and are not hard spending caps.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The initial German fixture exposed an unrelated untranslated no-browser-model status. Its advertised browser-model metadata now matches the standard E2E server; no fake model is loaded. The final rejection text itself translates and the fixture reports no interface translation gaps.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Capability detection and public diagnostics can share one conservative policy while returning no provider-controlled text. This preserves the coach's tool fallback instead of treating every request error as lack of tool support.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Recognized key shapes cannot cover an opaque provider credential or unknown private field. Fixed diagnostic vocabulary removes that reflection channel without needing to know every secret value or encoding.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Library-cache session cleanup (experimental)
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.11.1, the first bounded part of 11.4.2.11 / ASVS 14.3.1. The parent and its deviation remain open; the ASVS matrix stays at 40 verified, 26 not applicable, two deviations and two open.

nodes.text: - This is a separate reviewable cache/session submilestone. Active board/chat/drafts, private worker/index state, autosave provenance/migration, client departure/BFCache, automatic offline expiry and already loaded data in other tabs still require coordinated cleanup. Neither local cache deletion nor backend logout establishes complete client erasure. Keep TODO 11.4.2.11 and ASVS 14.3.1 unsatisfied with the original RC/final-release conditions and dates.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - An authoritative authentication failure must not enter the ordinary network-outage cache path. A generation check after persistence is too late to prevent resurrection: cancel transactions and check before starting writes, including writes reached through notification callbacks. Backend logout can succeed while local deletion is blocked, so retries must retain the acknowledgement and accurately report each outcome.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — LLM security evidence and reproduced open boundaries
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.3.11; implemented/tested local controls mapped for 11.3.1, 11.3.4–8. Parent 11.3 and categories 11.3.2/3/9/10 remain open.

nodes.text: - No model identity, source digest, legal line, matching citation or regex cue count certifies semantic correctness. Provider-side training/retention, operator filesystem ownership and hosted authentication remain separate trust decisions.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Review completion does not complete parent 11.3. Existing annotation, tool, vector and usage work made several old TODO notes stale, but configured-credential error leakage, mutable model identity, unrestricted prose and runtime-stream consumption gaps remain explicit. The next fix is the reproduced rejection leak, followed by independent stream bounds.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A zero recognized-error count is compatible with entirely false prose. The original “every chess claim” requirement cannot be marked complete from the existing checker or mock tests.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A provider timeout can stop connection/header work while a partially delivered body remains open. A total runtime deadline and response cap need their own implementation and regressions.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Credential separation on successful model requests does not imply safe provider-error reflection. Prefix redaction misses credentials without that syntax.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Local release review preparation
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.6 preparation; the release gate remains open.

nodes.text: - Prerequisites #118–#122 are merged; #123/#124 remain open at recording. Full browser CI is still running. This review preparation leaves the release candidate, TODO 11.6 approval and broader unsatisfied requirements separate; it does not establish ASVS compliance or authorize publishing.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A reviewable release decision needs exact evidence and individual unresolved conditions together. A passing feature check cannot supply an owner's risk disposition or evidence about a later merged revision.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Native checkout isolation (experimental)
nodes.annotation: TODO items: 11.4.2.9 and 11.4.2.9.1 / ASVS 13.4.1. The reviewed source and independent macOS/Linux/image evidence technically verify this control for the owner-selected final modes; this does not grant final-release approval.

nodes.text: - The owner explicitly selects macOS and Linux for the native final release (2026-10-25). Windows is outside that scope and refuses unsupported isolation. Source-pinned macOS/Linux and packaged verification passes for the selected final modes. Explicit HTTP development and legacy-origin recovery remain outside final scope. OS/bootstrap/runtime/directory writers stay trusted; do not count an altered runtime, deliberate metadata hard link or extra mount as a supported deployment. The filesystem policy is separate from network restrictions and hosted authentication.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Moving runtime files or hiding dot paths from HTTP does not stop a same-user process opening the original checkout. Node permissions also are not a malicious-code boundary, so verification must exercise the real OS restriction, including native SQLite. Isolation must preserve revocation semantics: a read-only file bind can silently retain an obsolete permission policy after the operator replaces its pathname.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Native HTTPS listener prerequisite
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.7.1; parent 11.4.2.7 and cookie migration 11.4.2.1 remain open.

nodes.text: - Native HTTPS is a prerequisite for the first cookie remediation; it does not implement secure prefixes or data-preserving migration. All twelve ASVS fix TODOs and their technical statuses stay open/unchanged, including final transport enforcement and actual endpoint/certificate evidence. The existing HTTP RC/development path is retained until the final deployment transition is implemented. No release or merge approval is implied.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - A working TLS listener and a secure deployment are different deliverables. Testing the real CLI avoids mistaking a wrapper's HTTPS support for application support, and checking identities before storage creation prevents failed transport setup from leaving new private databases behind.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Native-Origin checks and explicit SVG encoding
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.1. Remaining ASVS deployment deviations, TLS/inventory verification and release gates stay open.

nodes.text: - This does not add a trusted reverse proxy, CLI TLS mode, cookie-name migration, HSTS, hosted authentication or release approval. Local HTTP and the other ASVS deviations remain explicit.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Synthetic API-client Origins prove consistent server policy; they do not prove a browser CSRF exploit existed. JSON/non-safelisted headers and lack of CORS approval already provided a separate defense.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Scheme is part of an origin. A matching host cannot substitute for it, and client forwarding metadata cannot describe the native transport reliably.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - Header assertions on actual GET/HEAD responses and an SVG browser navigation verify the encoding boundary directly without treating a source constant as a sufficient test.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Object, PR-section and documentation assurance browser

nodes.text: - These levels add reference precision, not compliance or completion claims. Static calls do not prove runtime execution; dynamic/member calls, re-export chains and unsupported languages remain outside extraction. Exact object mentions require a cited file and unambiguous name in the same authored section/item. PR file membership never becomes an inferred object-level change claim.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Retained PR descriptions are refreshable snapshots because GitHub does not supply immutable body revisions. Review comments and CI logs are not fetched. Documentation extraction covers common headings and inline/full/collapsed reference links, with unsupported anchors and schemes recorded rather than guessed.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Lexical scope matters: a parameter that shadows a function name must not become a call edge to the containing function. Independent fixtures exposed and corrected that mapping before real data generation.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.text: - A replayable range and content hash let readers inspect exactly what an edge refers to. Keeping PR/file changes separate from section/object mentions preserves that precision when historical descriptions are incomplete.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Partial TLS transport inventory and reproducible probe (experimental)
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.6.1, a prerequisite under 11.4.2.6 / ASVS 12.1.1. The parent, encrypted-connectivity and public-trust controls remain open.

nodes.text: - This completes only the bounded evidence-collection prerequisite. Actual operator/browser/image/SDK/fetch/redirect transport evidence, configuration enforcement, public trust and renewal remain required. Legacy client refusal cannot establish remote downgrade refusal. All ASVS statuses/counts, RC decisions and original deadlines remain unchanged. No page/UI change or live model call.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - Negotiation, trust acceptance, client policy and server downgrade refusal are separate observations. A successful public-origin handshake is useful retained evidence but cannot certify an SDK path, a redirected model transfer or a private local installation.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Pin browser-model source revisions
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.3.3.1 complete; parent supply-chain review remains open.

nodes.text: - This review reads only public metadata, model-card/licence text and 134/135-byte LFS pointers. It neither downloads weights nor runs inference or a provider. Declared base-model lineage, quantization/training provenance and quality remain unverified; mutable cloud/Ollama/Chrome identities and TODO 11.3.3 stay open. nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.6 candidate preparation; the release gate remains open.

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Private position analysis without navigation URLs (experimental)
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.10 / ASVS 14.2.1. The reviewed implementation and cited verification technically address this control; the release gate and authenticated client-data lifecycle remain open.

nodes.text: - The external position deep link is removed in favour of local exploration. Separately exported data and third-party URL/retention choices belong to their own workflow. This change neither erases saved records/caches nor satisfies authenticated client-data lifecycle (11.4.2.11). Existing native/platform/TLS release conditions remain separate.

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Protected cookies with identity-preserving migration
nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.1 / ASVS 3.3.1. The other eleven ASVS remediations and final-release gate remain open.

nodes.text: - This is the cookie-protection fix, not authenticated sessions, HSTS, external-provider TLS inventory, public trust or release approval. Historical RC raw findings are unchanged. The remaining eleven ASVS fix TODOs stay open with their existing dates; CodeQL default-branch alerts are not manually dismissed.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The explicit HTTP development exception is retained with isolated names and synthetic/mock test use; it cannot adopt a production identity. The operator tools remain development clients and retain paid-call approval requirements. Browser JSON exports do not back up cookies or move browser storage across origins. Rollback uses a saved full profile and the tested HTTPS baseline, not a cookie-secret API or a database downgrade. No new dependency is added.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - The cookie name can change without re-keying either private store because ownership and accounting depend on the opaque value. Keeping the value makes recovery verifiable against the previous implementation; rejecting ambiguous identities prevents a convenience fallback from silently presenting an empty collection as lost data.
nodes.heading: Insights

nodes.title: 2026-10-25 — Rebuild PDFs by modification date

nodes.text: - Modification dates now decide freshness, as requested; touching a source rebuilds it even if its bytes are unchanged. Embedded image timestamps are not tracked: delete the affected PDF after changing only an image, as documented. Tool-version changes are not automatically detected.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.annotation: TODO item: 11.4.2.11.2, extending the cache boundary under 11.4.2.11 / ASVS 14.3.1. The parent remains unsatisfied, with 40 verified, 26 not applicable, two deviations and two open controls.

nodes.text: - This establishes common termination signalling/transport fences and derived-library cleanup; it does not clear every active board, private draft, worker/model context, rendered source or persisted autosave. Startup still restores legacy browser autosave before full ownership/migration. Complete departure/BFCache and private data already copied into DOM/RAM remain open. A failed marker write cannot promise durable intent after destruction, and suspended browsers cannot execute timer callbacks until resumed. Backend revocation, canonical records and provider-accepted work retain their own boundaries. Keep the original RC dates and final-release gate; do not upgrade ASVS 14.3.1.
nodes.heading: Deviations

nodes.text: - An independent client treating authentication failure as an ordinary outage can keep another client's private cache alive. A shared boundary needs both cancellation and result fences through the entire response, plus a nonauthorizing identity distinct from expiry. Offline termination needs an acknowledged local hint to prevent reuse across reloads; metadata persistence failure and cache deletion failure are different outcomes. Explicit data erasure must also coordinate its live in-memory observer to avoid immediately recreating erased keys.

`just offline`, a recipe of its own: on first run it downloads the chosen model's weights into `site/models/` (gitignored, checksums verified); then it builds and serves the app with local-only mode on and the in-browser model as the provider. Runtime:
    - WebLLM on WebGPU first: fast, with an OpenAI-style API and JSON-schema output
    - wllama when there's no WebGPU: llama.cpp in WebAssembly, multi-threaded under the COOP/COEP headers we already send
    - Chrome's built-in model (Prompt API) as an optional extra where it exists
    - Licences fit GPL-3.0 (Apache-2.0, MIT)
    - Default wllama covers WebGPU and WebAssembly without a second dependency. Optional Chrome Prompt API is selected explicitly with `BROWSER_RUNTIME=chrome` or `just offline-chrome`; browser-managed weights/resources and explicit Load-per-session requirements are documented separately

Model: a small open model under Apache-2.0 or MIT, chosen with the tutor eval set (3.8). It only puts into words what the engine and the detectors found, which is what makes a small model usable. The weights download on first use, only after the player agrees, with the size shown. They're cached in the browser and always come from our own server (2.16.0), never from a CDN. Done: Qwen2.5 1.5B Instruct (default) and 0.5B, Apache-2.0, pinned by SHA-256, consent before loading. The eval set (3.8) keeps 1.5B as the default: 50% against 42% for 0.5B, but far behind the cloud models (Haiku 79%, Opus 95%), so it stays the offline fallback

wllama runs in its own Worker behind the page-side sample interface; Chrome's current API requires Window access and uses disposable session clones. Settings list them as "In browser", and local-only mode (2.14) counts them as local

Resources: on the CPU it competes with Stockfish for threads, so the analyst gets fewer threads while the model is generating. Free memory is checked before loading, and the model is unloaded when idle

Interesting moves, not only the best: the analyst's MultiPV count and a centipawn window become settings. Engine tools for the coach: the model asks, and Stockfish and the motif detectors answer *(added)*

Tools:
    - `analyse(fen, depth, lines)`: the top lines in SAN, with evaluations
    - `try_move(fen, move)`: does this move work, and what refutes it (`go searchmoves`)
    - `threats(fen)`: what the opponent would play if it were their move (side to move flipped; not when in check)
    - `compare(fen, moves)`
    - `find_mate(fen, n)`
    - `find_motifs(fen, line)`: `moveMotifs` on every move of a line

Pattern search over lines: detectors inspect every move, with before/after engine evaluations and a short best-reply continuation confirming material gain, mate or sustained positional compensation. Unverified and refuted patterns are withheld. Candidate detectors cover the tactical themes in 6.2, including skewers, double checks, deflection, decoy, overloading, interference, removing a defender and checking zwischenzugs. A 1.5-pawn gap flags an "only move" when the best move still holds. Checks share an EPD cache and a search/time budget; see DONE.md for the conservative limits

Native tool calling in the gateway: Claude tool use, and function calling for OpenAI, Mistral and Ollama. One mechanism also serves load tools (4.8.3) and board tools (4.10.3). Only an explicit unsupported-tool rejection enables fixed-context fallback, scoped to the actual provider/model for that task and shown in the answer. Temporary or unrelated provider errors preserve tool access. A successful connection test retries support for that model

Where the engine runs: in the page, with the gateway handing each tool call to the page and waiting for the result, or on the server, where the npm Stockfish build also runs in Node. Decide on latency, cost and hosted load (10.1). Each answer gets a cap on tool calls and engine time. Decided: in the page. The page asks the gateway for one model turn at a time and runs each tool call on its own Stockfish

Tool arguments are untrusted: FENs and moves are checked with chess.js, and depth, time and line count are capped. Every line the model quotes must come from a tool result (3.4). The tool results are kept with the answer, so the chat can show the evidence

Tactics: 13 bilingual concept lessons covering forks, pins, skewers, discovered attacks, double checks, deflection, decoy, overloading, interference, removing a defender, zwischenzugs, back rank and mating patterns.
